result.title: Algorithmic drift in generative adaptive learning
result.summary: Generative artificial intelligence promises to democratize personalized tutoring, yet the longitudinal stability of adaptive systems remains under-theorized. Current ethical discourse focuses on static bias. This paper argues that a distinct threat lies in algorithmic drift: a feedback loop in which minor, demographically asymmetric observation errors compound over time into systemic inequities. We make three contributions. First, we formalize algorithmic drift as a coupled learner--tutor dynamical system. Second, we corroborate this theory with an agent-based Monte Carlo simulation in which either a transparent online tracker or an LSTM deep-knowledge-tracing network drives an IRT-based curriculum policy. Third, we introduce the temporal fairness stabilizer (TFS), a targeted intervention that periodically re-probes learner capability, and benchmark it against standard exploration baselines with explicit group-fairness metrics and replication-level inference. Within the modeled environment, TFS closes the achievement gap where generic exploration does not, and we characterize the conditions under which it succeeds. We separate what is established analytically, what is demonstrated in simulation, and what remains to be validated with real learners. Our results reframe algorithmic fairness in education as a temporal property of a closed loop rather than a deployment-time checkbox.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把「算法漂移」形式化为学习者—导师耦合动力系统，用基于 IRT 课程策略的蒙特卡洛仿真验证微小且群体不对称的观测误差如何随时间累积成系统性不平等，并提出周期性重新探测学习者能力的 temporal fairness stabilizer 作为干预。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「周期性重探以纠正闭环中累积的观测误差」与 LVR 中重新获取视觉证据、纠正 latent 状态漂移及何时 LOOK 的决策可能有概念对应，可供核查其闭环误差累积分析能否迁移到推理轨迹的贡献分配与停止判断。
